solution: The right angle of \(\Delta PQR\) is at \(R\), so the hypotenuse is the side opposite \(R\), namely \(PQ\); the two legs are \(PR\) and \(QR\). Taking \(\angle P\) as the reference angle, the leg opposite it is \(QR\). Sine is the opposite side over the hypotenuse, so \(\sin P = \frac{QR}{PQ}\).

The right angle of \(\Delta PQR\) is at \(R\), so the hypotenuse is \(PQ\) and the legs are \(PR\) and \(QR\). Taking \(\angle Q\) as the reference angle, the leg lying along it is \(QR\), so \(QR\) is the adjacent side. Cosine is the adjacent side over the hypotenuse, so \(\cos Q = \frac{QR}{PQ}\).

The right angle of \(\Delta PQR\) is at \(R\), so \(PQ\) is the hypotenuse and \(PR\), \(QR\) are the legs. Taking \(\angle P\) as the reference angle, the opposite leg is \(QR\) and the adjacent leg is \(PR\). Tangent is the opposite side over the adjacent side, so \(\tan P = \frac{QR}{PR}\).

The right angle of \(\Delta PQR\) is at \(R\), so \(PQ\) is the hypotenuse and \(PR\), \(QR\) are the legs. Taking \(\angle Q\) as the reference angle, the opposite leg is \(PR\) and the adjacent leg is \(QR\). Tangent is the opposite side over the adjacent side, so \(\tan Q = \frac{PR}{QR}\).

The right angle of \(\Delta XYZ\) is at \(Y\), so the hypotenuse is the side opposite \(Y\), namely \(XZ = c\); the legs are \(XY = b\) and \(YZ = a\). Taking \(\angle X\) as the reference angle, the leg opposite it is \(YZ = a\). Sine is the opposite side over the hypotenuse, so \(\sin X = \frac{YZ}{XZ} = \frac{a}{c}\).

The right angle of \(\Delta XYZ\) is at \(Y\), so \(XZ = c\) is the hypotenuse and the legs are \(XY = b\) and \(YZ = a\). Taking \(\angle Z\) as the reference angle, the opposite leg is \(XY = b\) and the adjacent leg is \(YZ = a\). Tangent is the opposite side over the adjacent side, so \(\tan Z = \frac{XY}{YZ} = \frac{b}{a}\).

The right angle of \(\Delta XYZ\) is at \(Y\), so \(XZ = c\) is the hypotenuse and the legs are \(XY = b\) and \(YZ = a\). Taking \(\angle X\) as the reference angle, the leg lying along it is \(XY = b\), so \(b\) is the adjacent side. Cosine is the adjacent side over the hypotenuse, so \(\cos X = \frac{XY}{XZ} = \frac{b}{c}\).

The right angle of \(\Delta XYZ\) is at \(Y\), so \(XZ = c\) is the hypotenuse and the legs are \(XY = b\) and \(YZ = a\). Taking \(\angle X\) as the reference angle, the opposite leg is \(YZ = a\) and the adjacent leg is \(XY = b\). Tangent is the opposite side over the adjacent side, so \(\tan X = \frac{YZ}{XY} = \frac{a}{b}\).

The right angle of \(\Delta LMN\) is at \(M\), so the hypotenuse is the side opposite \(M\), namely \(LN\); the legs are \(LM\) and \(MN\). Here \(\angle L = 50^\circ\), so \(\sin 50^\circ = \sin L\). The leg opposite \(\angle L\) is \(MN\), and sine is the opposite side over the hypotenuse, so \(\sin 50^\circ = \frac{MN}{LN}\).

The right angle of \(\Delta LMN\) is at \(M\), so \(LN\) is the hypotenuse and \(LM\), \(MN\) are the legs. Here \(\angle L = 50^\circ\), so \(\cos 50^\circ = \cos L\). The leg lying along \(\angle L\) is \(LM\), so it is the adjacent side, and cosine is the adjacent side over the hypotenuse. Hence \(\cos 50^\circ = \frac{LM}{LN}\).

The right angle of \(\Delta LMN\) is at \(M\), so \(LN\) is the hypotenuse and \(LM\), \(MN\) are the legs. Here \(\angle N = 40^\circ\), so \(\tan 40^\circ = \tan N\). The leg opposite \(\angle N\) is \(LM\) and the leg adjacent to it is \(MN\); tangent is the opposite side over the adjacent side, so \(\tan 40^\circ = \frac{LM}{MN}\).

The right angle of \(\Delta LMN\) is at \(M\), so \(LN\) is the hypotenuse and \(LM\), \(MN\) are the legs. Here \(\angle N = 40^\circ\), so \(\cos 40^\circ = \cos N\). The leg lying along \(\angle N\) is \(MN\), so it is the adjacent side, and cosine is the adjacent side over the hypotenuse. Hence \(\cos 40^\circ = \frac{MN}{LN}\).

The angle \(\alpha = \angle PRQ\) belongs to \(\Delta PQR\), whose right angle is at \(Q\) (given \(\angle PQR = 90^\circ\)). So the hypotenuse is the side opposite \(Q\), namely \(PR\), and the legs are \(PQ\) and \(QR\). Taking \(\alpha\) at vertex \(R\) as the reference angle, the opposite leg is \(PQ\) and the adjacent leg is \(QR\). Hence \(\sin \alpha = \frac{PQ}{PR}\), \(\cos \alpha = \frac{QR}{PR}\) and \(\tan \alpha = \frac{PQ}{QR}\).

The angle \(\theta = \angle QPS\) belongs to \(\Delta PQS\), whose right angle is at \(Q\) (given \(\angle PQS = 90^\circ\)). So the hypotenuse is the side opposite \(Q\), namely \(PS\), and the legs are \(PQ\) and \(QS\). Taking \(\theta\) at vertex \(P\) as the reference angle, the opposite leg is \(QS\) and the adjacent leg is \(PQ\). Hence \(\sin \theta = \frac{QS}{PS}\), \(\cos \theta = \frac{PQ}{PS}\) and \(\tan \theta = \frac{QS}{PQ}\).
